Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan: issue #6843, a CI triage for PR #6569 (`ai/issue-6568`)

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `f6b48d379aa34b095438456638eca6b21899108d`. The checkout is `main` (symbolic ref `main`). The issue has no integration-branch metadata, so the work targets `main`. There is no mismatch, so no `BLOCKED:` is needed.

Scope-mode: Selective Expansion
Reuse-audit: extends _run_validation_lint
Scope-mode justification: The issue names one stale assertion, at `tests/test_family_node_runtime.py:143`. The same node-runtime marker is also checked by source text at `tests/test_render_validation_templates.py:393`. If PR #6569 changes the node-runtime template to `printf`, that check breaks the same way, so it is in scope. Four other family-marker assertions use the same source-text pattern: `tests/test_render_validation_templates.py:148`, `:349` and `:461`, and `tests/test_family_python_repo_checks.py:128`. Changing all six to "run the rendered script and assert its stdout" costs well under 30 extra lines. It adds no dependency and no new interface. It also passes against both the `echo` templates on `main` and the `printf` form described for PR #6569. Under the Boil the Lake rule and §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), completeness supports correctness, so the plan takes the complete option. No template, workflow or script changes.

### Conflicts found (CONFLICT DETECTION)
- On the planning ref (`main`), `workflow-templates/validation-harness/node-runtime/tests/10_family_marker.sh.j2:5` still reads `echo "ok 1 - node-runtime family for {{ slots.project_name }}"`. The `printf 'ok 1 - %s family for %s\n'` form the triage cites exists only on PR #6569's head `b985e215`. That PR was not readable from this sandbox (no `gh`, no remote). The current assertion therefore passes on `main`. The fix must pass against both forms; it must not depend on either one.
- The triage infers which assertion fails; the log does not confirm it. A bare `assert` prints an empty message in `main()`.
- CI runs `tests/test_family_node_runtime.py` directly at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:787`. The other two test files have no direct `python3 tests/...` line in the workflows, so they presumably run under pytest collection.

### 1. Files likely to change
- `tests/test_family_node_runtime.py`: required.
- `tests/test_render_validation_templates.py`: the node-runtime site at `:393` is required for the PR to go green; the sites at `:148`, `:349` and `:461` are the selective expansion.
- `tests/test_family_python_repo_checks.py`: `:128`, selective expansion.
- No files are created. No templates, golden fixtures (`tests/fixtures/validation_harness/**`) or workflows change.

### 2. Functions / modules
- Add one module-level helper to each of the three test files, next to the existing `_run_renderer` / `_run_validation_lint`. The name `_run_family_marker` is unused in all three files (checked by grep):
  ```
  def _run_family_marker(script: Path) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
      subprocess.run(["bash", str(script)], cwd=str(script.parent),
                     text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=60,
                     env={**os.environ, "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1"})
  ```
  Use the same style as `_run_validation_lint`: tabs, a list argv, no `shell=True`.
- Replace each `family_*_text = ...read_text(...)` plus `assert "<family> family for demo-project" in family_*_text` pair with:
  - `marker = _run_family_marker(output_root / "tests" / "10_family_marker.sh")`
  - `assert marker.returncode == 0, f"family marker failed rc={marker.returncode}: {marker.stderr}"`
  - `assert "ok 1 - <family> family for demo-project" in marker.stdout.splitlines(), marker.stdout`
  - Optionally `assert "1..1" in marker.stdout.splitlines()`. Both forms emit that line.
- At `tests/test_render_validation_templates.py:391-393`, the `family_marker_text` read sits between the `env_text` and `repo_checks_text` reads. Keep those two reads and replace only the marker read and its assertion.
- Give every assertion an explicit message so `main()` prints useful text in place of an empty `FAIL name:`. This also fixes the observability gap the triage pointed out.

### 3. Data structures affected
None.

### 4. API / interface changes
None. These are test-only changes. Test function names stay the same, which keeps the CI step at `ci.yml:787` and the `main()` runners working.

## Decisions
### D1 — Execute the rendered marker script instead of matching its source text
- Chosen: render, run `bash 10_family_marker.sh`, and assert exit code 0 plus the exact `ok 1 - … family for demo-project` line in stdout.
- Alternatives considered: (a) update the substring to the `printf` source form, which would break on `main`, where the template still uses `echo`; (b) regex-match both source forms, which is brittle and still tests source text, not behavior.
- Why: it checks the behavior that matters (the TAP output). It works whether the template uses `echo` or `printf`, and it does not break the PR's shell quoting.

### D2 — Convert all six family-marker assertion sites, not just the cited one
- Chosen: change all six sites in the three test files.
- Alternatives considered: only `test_family_node_runtime.py:143`.
- Why: `test_render_validation_templates.py:393` asserts the identical node-runtime string and would fail on the next CI step once PR #6569 syncs. The other four sites share the same weakness, and the extra cost is a few lines.

### D3 — A per-file helper, not a shared test-utility module
- Chosen: one small `_run_family_marker` per file.
- Alternatives considered: a new `tests/_validation_harness_helpers.py`.
- Why: each of these files already defines its own `_run_renderer` and has no shared helper module. Adding one would be new structure (Layer 3) with no clear benefit.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundary: the test runs a script rendered from repo templates and fixed test slot values (`project_name: "demo-project"`). No untrusted input is involved.
- Execution uses a list argv, no `shell=True`, a 60 s timeout, and `cwd` inside the `TemporaryDirectory`. Nothing is written outside the temp tree.
- There are no new endpoints, credentials or money paths. The money-handling checks do not apply.
- Running the rendered script slightly strengthens the coverage that PR #6568/#6569 targets (shell quoting of slot values): a quoting regression that breaks execution now fails the test.

## Risks and edge cases
- On PR #6569 the marker template might source `_lib/tap_helpers.sh` or other helpers. Running it in place from `output_root/tests`, inside the fully rendered tree, keeps relative paths working. If it depends on container-only tools, the test would fail. `main`'s template needs only `bash`/`echo`, and the triage describes `printf`, a bash builtin. Low risk.
- `bash` must be on PATH. It is on CI runners and in the isolated editor container.
- This fix lands on `main`. PR #6569 goes green only after it syncs `main` (normal merge-train / sync flow). If PR #6569 also edited these test lines, the sync may conflict; the resolver handles that.
- The golden fixtures `tests/fixtures/validation_harness/*/tests/10_family_marker.sh` still contain `echo` lines. If PR #6569 also changed the python templates, any hash/golden comparison there is that PR's concern and out of scope here.

## Testing considerations
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_family_node_runtime.py`: both tests should print `PASS`.
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_render_validation_templates.py tests/test_family_python_repo_checks.py tests/test_family_node_runtime.py`
- `ruff check` on the three files, which should match CI's static-checks style. Indent with tabs, as the files already do.
- Optional local sanity check, not committed: temporarily change the node-runtime marker template to `printf 'ok 1 - %s family for %s\n' 'node-runtime' '{{ slots.project_name }}'`, confirm the tests still pass, then revert.
- No changelog fragment is expected, since this is a test-only change with no user-visible behavior. The implementer should follow CLAUDE.md §20 if it requires one for test changes.

Pre-execution self-check: the issue requirement (replace the source-text assertion with execution plus stdout and exit-code assertions) is covered. The plan is grounded in lines read on the planning ref. No external inputs are missing.

PLAN_SELF_CHECK: WARNING: The `printf` template form exists only on PR #6569's head and could not be read here; the fix is designed to pass against both `echo` and `printf`, but whether it turns that PR green is unverified until it syncs `main`.
